1.stem: [Conversation — Health Center] Why is the student calling the health center?

options.A: To refill a prescription the clinic gave him before.
options.B: To make an appointment about a persistent cough.
options.C: To get results from a test he had here last week.
options.D: To ask whether the clinic is open this weekend.

2.stem: [Conversation — student↔librarian] What does the librarian recommend to help the student narrow her search?

options.A: Ask her professor for a list of approved sources instead.
options.B: Come into the library in person to browse the printed policy journals on the shelves.
options.C: Read the two reserve books rather than searching the databases.
options.D: Use more specific keywords and apply filters for date and peer-review status.

3.stem: [Conversation — Dining Services] What does the staff member recommend as the safest option for the student?

options.A: Asking a chef to check ingredients at walk-up time
options.B: Reading the allergen cards carefully at each station
options.C: Switching to a meal plan that costs extra for safe meals
options.D: Ordering a day ahead from a dedicated allergen-free kitchen

4.stem: [Conversation — Library] Why does the student ask about getting notified when the book arrives?

options.A: The student doubts the clerk’s estimate that the book will arrive in a day or two.
options.B: The student wants to start using the book as soon as possible.
options.C: The student is unsure which of the two books she requested has not yet arrived.
options.D: The student is worried the book will be lost in transit between the two campuses.

5.stem: [Conversation — Writing Center] What does the tutor advise the student to do about the counterargument?

options.A: Add several new supporting points instead of going deeper.
options.B: Delete the counterargument so the essay has room to breathe.
options.C: Cut a weaker example and use the room to answer the objection.
options.D: Move the counterargument up into the introduction, right after the thesis.

6.stem: [Conversation — student↔librarian] What must the student do to reserve Room 410 for tomorrow?

options.A: Bring all group members to the library immediately.
options.B: Pay a reservation fee at the front desk.
options.C: Call the librarian to confirm the reservation.
options.D: Submit a special request form online by 5 p.m. today.

7.stem: [Conversation — International Student Office] Why does the student need to file the form?

options.A: She is switching to online-only courses and needs her advisor's signature for that.
options.B: She has already fallen out of status and must file the form to be reinstated.
options.C: She will drop below full-time enrollment to do an internship.
options.D: She is taking extra summer classes so that she can graduate a semester early.

8.stem: [Conversation — student and financial-aid officer about a scholarship deadline] According to the financial-aid officer, what happens if the recommendation letter is submitted after the deadline?

options.A: The application will not be considered at all.
options.B: The application will still be considered if the letter is only one day late.
options.C: The student will have to pay a late fee.
options.D: The student can request an extension.

9.stem: [Conversation — student and registrar about course-substitution rules] When is the deadline for submitting the course substitution form?

options.A: Before the student registers for STAT 220 in a later term.
options.B: At any time before the end of the current semester.
options.C: By the end of the add/drop period, Friday at 4 p.m.
options.D: Within two weeks of the request being submitted to the registrar.

10.stem: [Conversation — Residence hall] What is Student B’s attitude toward the new policy?

options.A: Initially reluctant, but ultimately supportive.
options.B: Immediately enthusiastic, before hearing any reason.
options.C: Opposed from the start and unmoved by the reasoning.
options.D: Unaware of what the policy actually requires.

11.stem: [Conversation — Campus Security] What can be inferred about why the officer will not release the laptop immediately?

options.A: The laptop is being held as evidence in an investigation.
options.B: The officer doubts the laptop actually belongs to the student.
options.C: The student's photo ID is locked inside the laptop case he can't yet access.
options.D: The library must first confirm the item was turned in.

12.stem: [Conversation — roommates] What do the roommates decide to do next?

options.A: Ask the landlord to fix the heating system first.
options.B: Accept the rent increase without question.
options.C: Look for other apartments and negotiate with their landlord.
options.D: Move out immediately to a cheaper place.

13.stem: [Conversation — Advisor Meeting] Why does the advisor suggest including the club's dues in the request?

options.A: Because dues are the only money the committee will accept.
options.B: Because the committee requires clubs to pay a fee.
options.C: Because the activities fund cannot cover the full amount.
options.D: Because contributing its own money signals the club's commitment.

14.stem: [Announcement — Transit] What should passengers do next?

options.A: Board the train immediately
options.B: Request a refund
options.C: Find alternative transportation
options.D: Wait for further announcements

15.stem: [Conversation — Friends] What does Speaker B imply about their weekend plans?

options.A: They are busy with academic work.
options.B: They have plans to visit the museum.
options.C: They are not interested in the museum.
options.D: They are free all weekend.

16.stem: [Conversation — student↔librarian] What does the librarian offer as a solution to the student's problem?

options.A: A first-floor room is free from three o'clock for the whole of the afternoon.
options.B: A room on the second floor is available for part of the requested time.
options.C: The group can use the nearby open seating area for the entire two-hour meeting.
options.D: The library will waive its start-and-end-time policy so the group can begin at three.

17.stem: [Conversation — Office hours] Why does the professor ask about the conclusion?

options.A: To identify areas needing further development.
options.B: To check if the sources were used correctly.
options.C: To ensure the student has completed it.
options.D: To assess the student's understanding of the paper.

18.stem: [Announcement — Transit] Why does the announcer say the delay is expected to be "about 45 minutes"?

options.A: To suggest that passengers bound for Boston take a later train
options.B: To confirm that the three o'clock train will now depart at exactly 3:45
options.C: To explain why the track maintenance could not be done overnight
options.D: To offer an estimate rather than a guaranteed departure time

19.stem: [Conversation — Campus] Why is the first speaker worried about the delay?

options.A: The shuttle may be cancelled for the rest of the day rather than delayed.
options.B: A commitment scheduled for that morning may be missed.
options.C: The bike-share stations are too far from campus to reach in time.
options.D: The roadwork causing the delay is expected to last for several more days.

20.stem: [Conversation — Advising] Why does the advisor suggest looking at the syllabi together?

options.A: To identify periods when assignments and exams might overlap.
options.B: To show that the debate club has to go if he takes eighteen credits.
options.C: To steer the student toward courses with lighter reading.
options.D: To persuade him to drop from eighteen credits to a lighter load.

21.stem: [Conversation — Tech Support] What does the technician say the student should do if the fix does not work?

options.A: Reset her student password again.
options.B: Switch to using the network on her phone instead.
options.C: Bring the laptop to the help desk in person.
options.D: Restart her laptop several times until it connects.

22.stem: [Conversation — Dining Services] What is the first thing the staff member tells the student she must do?

options.A: Register the allergy with the health center
options.B: Place a day-ahead order from the pantry
options.C: Pay a fee to unlock the allergen-free service
options.D: Email the allergen coordinator, Dev

23.stem: [Conversation — Library Help Desk] Why does the librarian suggest looking at a good article's reference list?

options.A: It reveals which of the separate databases the library actually subscribes to
options.B: It is a faster way to find other relevant sources than searching blindly
options.C: It is required in order to cite that article correctly in her finished paper
options.D: It shows whether the article she has found counts as a peer-reviewed source

24.stem: [Conversation — roommates] What agreement do the roommates reach by the end of the conversation?

options.A: They will take turns hosting friends, with each roommate getting alternate weekends.
options.B: They will stop inviting friends over for the rest of the semester, since both have big projects coming up.
options.C: They will set quiet hours after 10:00 p.m. on weekdays and post the rules on the fridge.
options.D: They will both move their studying into the living room and keep the bedrooms quiet.

25.stem: [Conversation — Service Desk] What does the student want to do at the lab?

options.A: Report that a machine in the lab is broken.
options.B: Sign up for a safety training session.
options.C: Reserve the confocal microscope for his project.
options.D: Return a piece of equipment he borrowed last week.

26.stem: [Conversation — IT Help Desk] What problem does the student describe?

options.A: He keeps getting disconnected from Wi-Fi in his dorm room
options.B: He cannot log in to the campus wireless network from either his laptop or his phone
options.C: He forgot the password he needs to register a wired connection on the campus portal
options.D: The Wi-Fi cuts out in the library whenever he tries to join one of his video calls

27.stem: [Conversation — Office hours] What does the professor want the student to do in the assignment?

options.A: Explain possible reasons for the trends in the data.
options.B: Summarize the instructions before beginning the analysis section.
options.C: List every number in the data set and describe what each one shows.
options.D: Compare this data set with the ones from the earlier assignments.

28.stem: [Conversation — Roommates] What is the conversation mainly about?

options.A: Arrangements the speakers make to sit down and work on the project together tonight.
options.B: The state of an assignment that one speaker still has to finish.
options.C: A disagreement over which of the two speakers should write the project's conclusion.
options.D: A plan to ask the instructor to postpone the due date.

29.stem: [Conversation — student and financial-aid officer about a scholarship deadline] What can be inferred about the state of the student’s application at the end of the conversation?

options.A: The officer will add the recommendation letter to the file herself if it arrives a day late
options.B: One required item is in someone else’s hands, so she cannot complete it on her own
options.C: The automated portal has already locked at five p.m., so none of her materials can be uploaded
options.D: She must start the whole application over because last year’s FAFSA is no longer valid

30.stem: [Conversation — Office Hours] Why does the professor mention that the counts happen at six-thirty in the morning?

options.A: To hint that the student may not be committed enough for it.
options.B: To point out that the city parks are emptiest that early in the morning.
options.C: To warn about a demanding condition that makes some students quit.
options.D: To explain that the city parks close later in the day.

31.stem: [Conversation — Gym] What is the student's main problem?

options.A: He was told a fitness class he signed up for is full
options.B: He wants to cancel a membership he no longer uses
options.C: He lost the ID card he needs to enter the gym
options.D: He was charged a membership fee he thought was included in tuition

32.stem: [Conversation — Library Help Desk] Why does the librarian tell the student to search the databases rather than the main catalog?

options.A: The databases are free through the portal, while the catalog charges per article
options.B: The main catalog is down for maintenance until later this week
options.C: The databases contain the journal articles, which the catalog does not
options.D: The catalog indexes only books published before the current academic year

33.stem: [Conversation — Office Hours] What is the main reason the student visits Professor Chen?

options.A: To request an extension on the final project now that the assignment has been returned.
options.B: To ask whether any extra credit is available to make up for the low assignment grade.
options.C: To discuss switching into a different section where the statistics work is lighter.
options.D: To get help understanding why their assignment grade was lower than expected.

34.stem: [Conversation — Bookstore] What will the student most likely do next?

options.A: Purchase the new edition and start the problem sets
options.B: File a refund request for her original order
options.C: Email the professor to ask about a conversion chart
options.D: Wait a week for a used old edition from the warehouse

35.stem: [Conversation — Office hours] Why does the advisor mention the journal 'Renewable Energy'?

options.A: To test the student's grasp of the subject area.
options.B: To emphasize how promising solar energy has become as a field
options.C: To point him to one particular article he should read first
options.D: To suggest a reliable source for current information

36.stem: [Conversation — Financial Aid] According to the officer, why was the student's grant reduced?

options.A: Her family's income rose enough to change her level of need
options.B: The grant program's total funding was cut for the coming year
options.C: She missed the deadline to file an Enrollment Status Update
options.D: She dropped below full-time enrollment for one semester
